# horsie_mcp_server (Resource)

A remote MCP server an agent preset can be granted.

Its tools are namespaced `mcp__<name>__<tool>`, so the name is part of what a preset refers to and not just a label.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "horsie_mcp_server" "linear" {
  name = "linear"
  url  = "https://mcp.linear.app/mcp"

  auth {
    kind  = "bearer"
    token = var.linear_token
  }
}

resource "horsie_mcp_server" "docs" {
  name = "docs"
  url  = "https://docs.example.com/mcp"

  # Public server: say so, rather than leaving the block out.
  auth {
    kind = "none"
  }
}

resource "horsie_mcp_server" "github" {
  name = "github"
  url  = "https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/"

  # Reuses horsie's existing GitHub App connection; no credential is stored here.
  auth {
    kind = "github_app"
  }
}

resource "horsie_agent" "triage" {
  name        = "triage"
  model       = horsie_model.sonnet.alias
  mcp_servers = [horsie_mcp_server.linear.name, horsie_mcp_server.github.name]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Stable id, and the prefix its tools are namespaced under. Changing it replaces the resource: horsie has no rename, and a silent move would strand every preset that granted the old name.
- `url` (String) Streamable-HTTP endpoint.

### Optional

- `auth` (Block, Optional) How horsie authenticates to the server. **Required** — say `kind = "none"` for a public server rather than leaving it out, so an unauthenticated call is a decision in the configuration rather than an omission. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--auth))

### Read-Only

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the last connect succeeded and the server is usable. Set by horsie, not here — a server is enabled by working, not by being asked to.
- `last_error` (String) Why the last connect failed, when it did.
- `tool_count` (Number) Tools advertised at the last successful connect.

<a id="nestedblock--auth"></a>
### Nested Schema for `auth`

Required:

- `kind` (String) One of `none`, `bearer`, `github_app` or `oauth`. Each kind reads only the attributes it needs; setting one it does not use is an error rather than being silently ignored.

Optional:

- `authorization_endpoint` (String) `oauth`: override discovery when the server publishes no metadata (RFC 9728 / 8414).
- `client_id` (String) `oauth`: a pre-registered client id. Omit to let horsie register one dynamically (RFC 7591), in which case the id it was issued appears here.
- `client_secret` (String, Sensitive) `oauth`: the client secret. Omit to keep, `""` to clear.
- `registration_endpoint` (String) `oauth`: as `authorization_endpoint`.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) `bearer`: the static token. Omit to leave a stored token untouched, or set `""` to clear it.
- `token_endpoint` (String) `oauth`: as `authorization_endpoint`.

Read-Only:

- `connected` (Boolean) `oauth`: whether an access token has been obtained. Terraform can write the client configuration but cannot complete the sign-in, which is a browser redirect — so a freshly applied `oauth` server is `connected = false` until someone authorises it from horsie's settings page.
- `has_client_secret` (Boolean) Whether an OAuth client secret is stored.
- `has_token` (Boolean) Whether a bearer token is stored. The server never returns the token itself.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Servers are addressed by name. Secrets are not returned, so an imported
# bearer or OAuth server needs its token written back into the configuration.
terraform import horsie_mcp_server.example linear
```
